title: Circular Import
code:
# In a.py:
import b
# In b.py:
import a

bugs.fix:
# Move shared logic to a separate module c.py
# and import from c in both a.py and b.py
bugs.explanation: Circular imports occur when two modules import each other. Python partially initializes the first module when the second tries to import it, causing `ImportError` or `AttributeError`. Refactor shared code into a third module.

title: re.match vs re.search
code:
import re
result = re.match(r'world', 'hello world')
print(result)

bugs.explanation: `re.match` only matches at the start of the string. `'hello world'` does not start with `'world'`, so `result` is `None`. Use `re.search` to find the pattern anywhere in the string.
